parameters.query: select id as tenant_id from tenants where slug = $1 and status = 'active';

nodes.name: Fetch Website
nodes.notes: TODO after import: confirm in n8n's UI that Response Format is set to 'text'/'String' (not JSON) so the raw HTML lands as a string, not a parse error. A User-Agent header is set since some sites reject requests without one; some sites will still block this entirely (bot detection, login walls, JS-only rendering) -- that's a real, unfixed limitation of a simple server-side fetch, not a bug.

parameters.query: insert into documents (tenant_id, title, source_type, source_url, status) values ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'processing') returning id as document_id;

nodes.name: Embed Chunk (Voyage AI)
nodes.notes: Runs once per chunk item (n8n's default per-item execution for HTTP Request nodes). batchInterval adds a small delay between calls to stay well under Voyage's rate limits on free tier -- tune this down if ingestion feels slow and you're not hitting rate limit errors.

parameters.query: insert into document_chunks (tenant_id, document_id, chunk_index, content, embedding) values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5::vector);
update documents set status = 'ready' where id = $1;

nodes.name: Mark Document Ready
nodes.notes: This node runs once per incoming chunk item (n8n re-triggers it per item since it's downstream of a multi-item branch), so the UPDATE fires multiple times for a multi-chunk document. That's harmless (idempotent -- same value each time) but worth knowing; a cleaner version would aggregate first. Flagged, not blocking.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { document_id: $('Create Document Row').first().json.document_id, status: 'ready', chunks_created: $('Chunk Text').all().length } }}
